## 01f4294de005

Concrete morphology shortcut: every ordinary generated sample has an all-zero row 1 because the placement code reserves both row 0 and row 1 before growing body blobs. In a 5,000-sample deterministic probe, row 1 was blank in 5,000/5,000 draws. All three canonical input pairs instead have nonzero body cells in row 1.

This allows a generated-data shortcut that segments “legend above the first blank row, body below it,” rather than learning that the legend is specifically the first row. A lawful counterexample is already present in canonical train pair 0, where `input[1][0] == 7`. The generator should allow body objects immediately below the legend while preventing actual component merging by local occupancy checks rather than a globally blank separator row.
